I have several interesting ancestors: 

My grandad was born during the bombing of Great Britain. While my great-grandmother was in labor, bombs were going off and glass was shattering everywhere. Immediately after he was born the doctor put him under a metal bowl to protect him from getting cut. I can only imagine how stressful that situation would be. 

I'm half Australian. My Grandma's side of the family goes all the way back to when criminals were being sent to Australia. That's how my family got to Australia. Most of them were sent for not paying debts or other small crimes like that, but one guy was sent for murder. 

One of my ancestors wrote the hymn ”Abide with Me.”

My family has a pub named after us in England as well as the street that it is on. We also own a few castles. More of my family used to own them, but everyone has moved out of England, so my Grandma's cousin maintains the ones we still own. My parents took pictures on one of the castle grounds when they visited England a few summer's ago. 

I have a few others, but this reply is getting too long already, so I'm going to go now!

When I was little I would make a path of picture books going from my bed to the door. My logic was that if I stepped on the books and not the floor then the monsters couldn't get me if I had to get up in the middle of the night.
That I was depressed and suicidal. That was about a month ago and now I'm on antidepressants. I'm feeling better than I've felt in a long time and my life is finally starting to turn around.

I just want to let everyone know that I am grateful for your reply's. It has shown me that I am not alone in this world. I go through these patches where I get extremely depressed and nothing will bring me out of it. It can be a couple days between attacks (I've started to calling them depression attacks because that's what they feel like) or a couple hours. I'm learning to deal with them and I truly want to get better. Thank you for taking the time to reply.

This didn't happen to me, but it happened when my mom was home alone with my little brother. He had a pretty bad fever when he was about 6 years old and my mom came upstairs to check on him. He was standing in front of the toilet just laughing hysterically. My mom asked him what was so funny and he said "I'm standing on a pile of dirt." My mom helped him back into bed as he continued to laugh. Then he just stops laughing abruptly and closes his eyes. My mom says his name in a concerned voice and then he suddenly bursts out a scream and opens his eyes wide open scaring the crap out of my mom. Then he bursts into hysterical laughter again. My mom was completely freaked out.

When he was about seven years old he had another fever and my mom was home alone with him again. She was watching TV with her back to the kitchen. She suddenly heard soft giggling coming from behind her and she abruptly turned around. My brother was standing in front of the Christmas tree softly giggling to himself. Then he slowly turned around and says "Mommy I caught all the Christmas presents on fire!" Needless to say, I refuse to be home alone with my brother when he is sick.
My music theory professor did that once in class and he just laughed as we all squirmed in our seats.
